Start hereGitHub Action

22 minutes read

GitHub Action

Offing's reusable Action scans the checked-out repository locally, emits GitHub annotations for findings, compares against an optional baseline, enforces a severity gate, and uploads the versioned JSON result.

What it looks like

One comment per pull request, updated in place on every re-run, with the severity counts, the top findings, and their exact location. Each row links to the source the rule cites, so a reviewer can check the claim before changing code.

Pull-request workflow

name: Offing

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  lifecycle:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: velella-sh/offing@v0.1.0
        with:
          baseline: .offing-baseline.json
          fail-on-severity: high

Version tags provide stable release references. Pin a full commit SHA when your threat model requires immutable third-party action references. A release tag points at a commit that carries the compiled Action bundle, which the release chain builds onto a release/<tag> branch and never rebuilds, so the Action runs without installing anything and a tag you pinned keeps doing what it did. Releasing explains why the bundle is not on main.

Reusable workflow (one uses: line)

Organizations that want the same scan in every repository without copying checkout and Action steps can call the reusable workflow instead. It checks out the caller, runs Offing with the common inputs, and needs only contents: read. The Action version is pinned inside the workflow file, so pinning the workflow pins the scanner.

name: Offing

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 4 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  lifecycle:
    uses: velella-sh/offing/.github/workflows/offing-reusable.yml@v0.8.0
    with:
      baseline: .offing-baseline.json
      fail-on-severity: high

Version. The reusable workflow first ships in v0.8.0. Until that tag exists, call @main only to try it, then replace it with the release tag before relying on it.

Every workflow input is optional and matches the Action default of the same name. Pass only what you need to change:

Workflow input Default Meaning
path . Repository root or subdirectory to scan.
paths empty Multi-line list of directories or globs relative to path.
baseline empty Baseline path relative to path.
baseline-warn-days 14 Warn when a baseline suppression expires within this many days.
on-expired resurface resurface or fail after a suppression's expires day.
min-support-days empty Warn on lines whose support ends within this many days.
fail-on-severity high Lowest failing level: none, info, low, medium, high, or critical.
mode scan scan or diff (diff fetches full history for the base and head SHAs).
annotations empty changed, all, or none; empty keeps the Action default.
report-name offing-report Artifact name when upload-report is true.
upload-report true Upload the JSON report as an Actions artifact.
attribution true Credit Offing in the job summary.

The workflow exposes the same result outputs as the Action (report-path, finding-count, has-new-findings, highest-severity, next-eol-date, findings-json) so a later job can branch on them. Features that need write permissions — pr-comment, suggest-fixes, commands, fix-pr, tracking-issue, upload-sarif, upload-badge — stay on the Action step above; the reusable workflow keeps the minimal contents: read permission set.

For an organization .github repository that offers the starter in the Actions "New workflow" gallery, copy templates/workflows/ into that repository's workflow-templates/ directory. See Organization rollout.

SHA-pinned actions

For the first-party actions covered by Offing, a full 40-character commit pin is classified in this order:

  1. A trailing release comment, such as # v4, # v4.1.1, # tag=v4.1.1, or # version: v4.1.1.
  2. Offing's bundled map of exact release-tag SHAs, when the pin has no trailing comment.
- uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2

A malformed, ambiguous, or conflicting comment is not replaced by a map lookup: Offing reports it as invalid-version-comment. A SHA absent from the bundled map is reported as unknown-sha. These references are not lifecycle findings, so they do not affect severity gates or annotations.

The uploaded JSON report records the total in unclassified.count and lists each reference with its action, SHA, reason, and workflow location under unclassified.references. CLI text output adds a one-line count when any exist. Classification uses only repository contents and the bundled map; scans make no network requests.

Create and commit the baseline locally when existing findings are accepted:

npx @velella/offing baseline . --output .offing-baseline.json

A baseline entry can also say why a finding is accepted and until when. These fields are all optional, so a baseline written without them keeps working, and they never change which findings are suppressed:

{ "fingerprint": "…", "ruleId": "nodejs.runtime.eol-20", "path": "package.json",
  "owner": "platform-team", "reason": "Upgrade tracked in PLAT-12", "created": "2026-10-17", "expires": "2027-01-31" }

owner and reason are non-empty text (up to 500 characters); created and expires are calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD), and expires is not before created. An entry with a malformed field makes the baseline fail to load, with the entry's position in the message. The schema is schemas/baseline.v1.schema.json. Expiry warnings. When a scan uses a baseline, every suppression that matched a finding and expires within the next 14 days is listed in the scan's diagnostics (and as a warning on the Action run), soonest first, with its owner and reason:

Baseline suppression expires in 5 days (2026-10-22): nodejs.runtime.eol-18 at package.json (owner: platform-team; reason: Upgrade tracked in PLAT-12).

Change the window with --baseline-warn-days <n> on offing scan or the baseline-warn-days Action input (0 to 365). The comparison day is today in UTC; --today YYYY-MM-DD sets it explicitly, which makes a run reproducible; suppression dates are compared only with that day.

After expires. A suppression is in force through its expires day and expired from the next day. An expired suppression stops hiding its finding: the finding is reported again, and the diagnostics say which suppression expired, how long ago, and its owner and reason. What happens beyond that is a policy, --on-expired on offing scan or the on-expired Action input:

Policy Behavior
resurface (default) The finding is back in the results and is judged by the usual severity gate.
fail The finding is back, and the scan also fails (the CLI exits 1, the Action fails the job) if any suppression has expired, even when the finding is below the gate.

Only entries with an expires can expire, so a baseline written before these fields behaves exactly as before. A finding stays hidden while at least one of its suppressions is in force.

Seeing what a baseline does. A scan that uses a baseline never hides suppressions silently. offing scan --json adds a suppressions object to the result (and scan.v1.schema.json documents it): how many findings the baseline hid, the day it compared with, and the expiring and expired suppressions with their rule, path, expires day, owner, and reason. The text report ends its findings with a line such as Baseline: 3 findings suppressed, 1 expiring within 14 days, 0 expired., the Action's job summary shows the same line and a table of the expiring and expired suppressions, and the MCP scan_repository tool returns the object when it is given a baseline. A scan without a baseline has no suppressions field.

Upgrading needs no migration. A baseline written by an earlier version (the offing.baseline.v1 schema, with only fingerprint, ruleId, and path) loads and suppresses exactly what it always did; a test loads a baseline written by the published 0.1.0 against the current scanner. Fingerprints do not depend on the new fields, so adding an owner or reason to an existing entry by hand does not change what it suppresses. A newer release can report findings that an older baseline never recorded (for example a rule added since); those appear as new, which is the point of a baseline.

The Action then annotates and gates only findings not represented by that baseline.

Chat and webhook digests

offing scan --format slack, --format teams, and --format webhook print a JSON payload to standard output. Offing only renders the payload and never sends it: the network call belongs to a step you write, so the scan itself stays offline.

  • slack is a Slack incoming-webhook message: a fallback text, a header, a counts summary, and one section per finding. It fits Slack's 50-block and 3,000-character section limits.
  • teams is a Microsoft Teams message with an Adaptive Card (version 1.4) for a Teams workflow webhook.
  • webhook is a generic JSON payload (schemaVersion: "offing.webhook.v1") with a count per severity and every finding, for any system that accepts JSON.

The chat formats list at most 20 findings, most severe first, and say how many were left out; webhook lists them all. Output is deterministic, with no timestamps in the chat formats.

Pipe the payload into your own webhook step. The URL lives in a secret, and the step runs only where you choose:

- uses: actions/checkout@v7
- run: npm ci   # your project must already depend on offing
- name: Post digest to Slack
  if: always()
  run: npx --no-install offing scan . --format slack | curl -sS -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data @- "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"
  env:
    SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}

Use --format teams with a Teams workflow URL, or --format webhook with any endpoint, in the same way.

Inputs and outputs

Every input is optional. The values below are the defaults used when a workflow does not provide a with entry.

Input Default Meaning
path . Repository root or subdirectory to scan; . is the checked-out repository.
paths empty Multi-line list of directories or globs (for example packages/*) relative to path. Each match is scanned in one run; findings go into one report and SARIF, with a job-summary section per package. Empty scans only path.
baseline empty Baseline path relative to path (or to each matched package when paths is set). Empty reports every finding; a configured path that is missing fails the Action.
min-support-days empty Warn (medium severity) on lines whose support ends within this many days; off when empty.
baseline-warn-days 14 Warn when a baseline suppression expires within this many days (0 to 365).
on-expired resurface What a baseline suppression does after its expires day: resurface (its finding is reported again) or fail (also fail the job).
fail-on-severity high Lowest failing level: none, info, low, medium, high, or critical.
mode scan scan scans the checked-out tree. diff compares the pull request base and head SHAs from the event payload and fails only on findings the pull request introduces. See pull request diff mode.
annotations empty Which findings become workflow annotations: changed annotates only findings on lines the pull request added or changed (the default in diff mode), all annotates every finding (the default in scan mode), none emits no annotations. Findings left out stay counted in the summary and the JSON report.
report-name offing-report Artifact name for the JSON report when upload-report is true.
upload-report true Upload the JSON report as an Actions artifact. false keeps the generated report only on the runner.
upload-sarif false Set to true to upload the findings to GitHub code scanning as SARIF. Needs security-events: write.
upload-badge false Generate a Shields.io endpoint JSON and a branded SVG badge, and upload both as the offing-badge artifact (14 days).
pr-comment false Set to true to post one summary comment on pull requests (counts and the top findings). Re-runs update the same comment. Needs pull-requests: write.
agent-authors Copilot, google-labs-jules[bot], devin-ai-integration[bot], chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], claude[bot] Comma-separated logins treated as coding agents. In diff mode, when the pull request author matches, the comment adds the Stale choices this agent introduced section. Set to none to turn it off. Matching ignores case and a leading @.
suggest-fixes false In diff mode, post one review whose suggestion blocks apply the deterministic fixes for findings on lines the pull request changed. Re-runs update the same review. Needs pull-requests: write; pull requests from forks are skipped.
commands false Set to true to answer /offing explain and /offing ignore comments when the workflow runs on issue_comment. Replies only to owners, members, and collaborators. Needs pull-requests: write.
fix-pr false Set to true to open or update one pull request on offing/fixes with every deterministic fix, and close it when nothing is left to fix. Runs only on schedule and workflow_dispatch events. Needs contents: write and pull-requests: write. See scheduled fix pull request.
tracking-issue false Set to true in a scheduled workflow to keep one issue listing findings by end-of-life date. Re-runs update the same issue; it closes when nothing is left and reopens when findings return. Needs issues: write.
github-token ${{github.token}} Token used to post the comment, command reply, or fix suggestions when pr-comment, commands, or suggest-fixes is true, to open, update, or close the fix pull request when fix-pr is true, and to update the tracking issue when tracking-issue is true.
attribution true Adds one line to the job summary saying the scan was done by Offing, with a link. Set to false to leave it out.
Output Availability Meaning
report-path Always Absolute runner path to the generated JSON report, whether or not upload-report is enabled.
finding-count Always Number of findings remaining after baseline comparison, encoded as a decimal string.
has-new-findings Always true when at least one finding remains after baseline comparison, false otherwise. In diff mode it covers the findings the pull request introduces.
highest-severity Always The highest remaining severity (info, low, medium, high, or critical), or empty when there are no findings.
next-eol-date Always The earliest end-of-life date among the remaining findings (YYYY-MM-DD), or empty when no finding carries a deadline.
findings-json Always The remaining findings as one compact JSON array. Each entry has id, ruleId, severity, title, path, and line and deadline when known.
badge-path When upload-badge is true Absolute runner path to offing-badge.json; otherwise empty.
badge-svg-path When upload-badge is true Absolute runner path to offing-badge.svg, next to the JSON; otherwise empty.
sarif-path When upload-sarif is true Absolute runner path to the generated SARIF file; otherwise empty.

The job summary shows how many findings there are per severity, the ten most severe findings with their location and a link to the evidence each one cites, the age of the lifecycle data, and a warning when the data is stale. When there are more than ten findings, it says how many more there are; the JSON report artifact lists them all.

Branching on results

The outputs describe the findings that remain after baseline comparison, so a later step can act on them without reading the report. Every value is empty or false when nothing remains.

Output Example value Meaning
has-new-findings true true when at least one finding remains, false otherwise.
highest-severity critical The most severe remaining level, or empty when there are none.
next-eol-date 2026-09-23 The earliest deadline among the remaining findings, or empty when none is dated.
findings-json [{"id":"…","ruleId":"…","severity":"high","title":"…","path":"package.json","line":4,"deadline":"2026-09-23"}] The remaining findings as one compact JSON array.

The scan step must pass for the steps after it to run, so this example sets fail-on-severity: none and leaves the decision to the later steps:

- uses: velella-sh/offing@v0
  id: offing
  with:
    fail-on-severity: none
- name: Note new findings
  if: steps.offing.outputs.has-new-findings == 'true'
  run: echo "Offing found new findings; highest severity is ${{ steps.offing.outputs.highest-severity }}."
- name: Warn about the next deadline
  if: steps.offing.outputs.next-eol-date != ''
  run: echo "The next end of life is ${{ steps.offing.outputs.next-eol-date }}."
- name: List finding ids
  run: echo '${{ steps.offing.outputs.findings-json }}' | jq -r '.[].id'

In diff mode the same outputs cover only the findings the pull request introduces, so findings-json lists what the pull request added rather than the whole backlog.

Monorepo paths

Monorepos should not need one job per package. Set paths to a multi-line list of directories or globs under path. Offing scans each match, writes one combined JSON report and SARIF, and adds one job-summary section per package. fail-on-severity is evaluated across all packages together.

- uses: actions/checkout@v7
- uses: velella-sh/offing@v0
  with:
    paths: |
      packages/*
      apps/web
    fail-on-severity: high

Literals must exist and be directories. A glob that matches nothing fails the Action. * and ? stay inside one path segment; ** crosses segments. Diff mode ignores paths and compares the whole pull request checkout instead.

High and critical findings become error annotations, medium findings become warnings, and low or informational findings become notices. The gate is evaluated independently from annotation level.

Pull request comment

Set pr-comment: true to get the comment shown at the top of this page: the counts per severity and the top findings, instead of reading every annotation. The same comment is updated on each re-run. The scan itself stays offline; only posting the comment calls the GitHub API.

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v6
  - uses: velella-sh/offing@v0
    with:
      pr-comment: "true"

Pull requests from forks get a read-only token, so the comment cannot be posted there: the Action logs a warning and the scan result is unaffected.

Agent-authored pull requests

When mode: diff and the pull request author is a coding agent, the comment also carries a Stale choices this agent introduced section. It lists each finding the pull request introduced with its path:line, rule title, replacement, and evidence link, and closes with the line the agent can act on: "Replace these and push again; Offing will re-check." The comment is still the one Offing comment, updated on re-runs; a second comment is never posted.

agent-authors takes a comma-separated list of logins. The default covers GitHub's Copilot coding agent (Copilot), Jules (google-labs-jules[bot]), Devin (devin-ai-integration[bot]), OpenAI Codex cloud (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]), and Claude (claude[bot]). Matching ignores case and a leading @. Set agent-authors: none to turn the section off, or name the logins your agents author with. The author comes from the event payload, so no extra request is made; scans stay offline.

Comment commands

Set commands: "true" and run the Action on issue_comment so a reviewer can ask about a finding or accept it without leaving the pull request. A short workflow of its own is enough; it can sit next to the scan workflow:

name: Offing commands

on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  answer:
    if: github.event.issue.pull_request != null
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.issue.number }}/head
      - uses: velella-sh/offing@v0
        with:
          commands: "true"

/offing explain <finding-id> replies with the finding, its location, replacement and deadline, the affected usages, and a link to every source. Take the id from an annotation's Finding: line, or from offing scan . --json.

/offing ignore <finding-id> <reason> replies with a baseline entry that is ready to review and commit, for example:

{ "fingerprint": "…", "ruleId": "nodejs.runtime.eol-20", "path": "package.json",
  "reason": "Upgrade tracked in PLAT-12", "created": "2026-10-29", "expires": "2027-01-27" }

Nothing is pushed. The reviewer adds the entry to the file named by the baseline input (.offing-baseline.json when it is empty) and commits it. The entry hides the finding until expires, 90 days after the reply; after that the finding is reported again, and on-expired: fail fails the job as well.

Comment text is untrusted input. Offing reads the first line that starts with /offing, parses it, and never evaluates it; file paths and ids from the comment are rendered as code, never as links. A reply is written only when the comment's author_association is OWNER, MEMBER, or COLLABORATOR; a command from anyone else, or a comment on an issue rather than a pull request, is skipped and logged as a notice. The finding comes from a local scan of the checked-out pull request head, so the scan stays offline and runs no repository code. Each reply carries a hidden marker and is updated on a re-run instead of being posted twice.

Lifecycle tracking issue

Set tracking-issue: true to keep one issue that lists what ends soon, without gating a build. On schedule and workflow_dispatch runs the Action finds the issue by a hidden marker, updates it, or creates it. Findings are sorted by end-of-life date with a link to the exact file and line, and a "Changed since the last run" table names what appeared and what is gone. When a scan finds nothing, the issue closes with an explanatory body; the next run that finds a lifecycle risk reopens it.

name: Offing lifecycle tracking
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 7 * * 1" # Mondays 07:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
concurrency:
  group: offing-tracking-issue
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  track:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: velella-sh/offing@v0.1.0
        with:
          tracking-issue: "true"
          fail-on-severity: none # the issue is the signal; do not fail the schedule

The marker is a hidden HTML comment, so the issue body stays readable and a re-run recognizes its own issue. The previous run's findings live in another hidden marker; that snapshot is how the next run says what changed. Do not edit or delete the markers: without them the next run creates a new issue. The scan stays offline; only updating the issue calls the GitHub API, and the job needs issues: write. Pull request tokens are read-only, so the input acts only on schedule and workflow_dispatch runs.

The Action looks for its issue among the 1,000 most recently updated issues. On a repository with more issue activity than that while the tracking issue is closed, it can fall outside the window and a second issue is created; delete one and the next run updates the other. GitHub caps issue bodies at 65,536 characters, so the findings table is shortened when needed while the hidden snapshot keeps tracking every finding; if even the shortened body would exceed the cap, the Action logs a warning and leaves the issue unchanged.

Pull request diff mode

finding-count and the severity gate cover every finding in the checkout. On a busy repository that backlog grows, so reviewers cannot see which findings a pull request actually introduced. mode: diff fixes that: the Action scans the pull request base and head refs with the same engine as offing diff, and the gate, annotations, badge, comment, and summary count only what the pull request introduced. Findings the pull request fixes are listed in a "Fixed by this pull request" table in the summary and the pull request comment.

steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    with:
      fetch-depth: 0   # diff mode archives the base and head SHAs from git objects, so fetch their history
  - uses: velella-sh/offing@v0
    with:
      mode: diff

The base and head come from the pull_request event payload (pull_request.base.sha and pull_request.head.sha); the comparison stays offline — both refs are unpacked with git archive and scanned locally. Outside a pull_request event, or when the payload lacks those SHAs, the Action logs a notice and runs a regular scan instead. The baseline input does not apply in diff mode: it describes accepted findings in the whole repository, not in one pull request, and the Action says so with a notice. Because the gate judges only introduced findings, a pull request that adds a deprecated package fails and one that only edits documentation passes.

Annotations on untouched files are noise, so diff mode annotates only findings on lines the pull request added or changed and counts the others in one summary line with a link to the full report. The gate, the severity counts, the badge, the comment, and the JSON report still cover every introduced finding. Set annotations: all to annotate every introduced finding, or annotations: none to emit no annotations at all. Scan mode defaults to all; an explicit annotations: changed there falls back to all with a notice because there is no pull request range.

Suggested fixes

Set suggest-fixes: true with mode: diff to let a reviewer accept a fix with one click instead of reading migration notes. For findings on lines the pull request added or changed that offing fix can repair deterministically, the Action posts one review whose comments each contain a suggestion block, so GitHub's Apply suggestion rewrites the line. Findings without a deterministic fix get no suggestion; the scan, the gate, and the report are unchanged.

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    with:
      fetch-depth: 0   # diff mode archives the base and head SHAs from git objects
  - uses: velella-sh/offing@v0
    with:
      mode: diff
      suggest-fixes: "true"

A re-run updates the review it left instead of adding another: the review body and the comments on the same file and lines are rewritten, and comments whose suggestion no longer applies are deleted. A suggestion at a new line arrives as one more review, because GitHub does not allow adding comments to a submitted review. Pull requests from forks get a read-only token, so the Action logs a notice and posts nothing. The scan itself stays offline; only posting the review calls the GitHub API.

End-of-life reminder issue

examples/lifecycle-watch.yml is a copyable starter that reminds a team before a deadline without anyone running a scan. Copy it to .github/workflows/lifecycle-watch.yml. Every Monday (and on demand) it scans with min-support-days, then opens one issue listing each line whose support ends within WINDOW_DAYS (default 90). The next run updates that same issue instead of opening another, and closes it when nothing is near its deadline.

The scan stays offline; only the final step calls the GitHub API. The job needs contents: read and issues: write, and sets fail-on-severity: none so the schedule does not fail. Change WINDOW_DAYS or the cron line to taste.

Scheduled fix pull request

Dependabot, but for end of life. Set fix-pr: true on a scheduled workflow and the Action keeps one pull request that contains every fix Offing can apply deterministically, the same patches offing fix prints. It commits them to offing/fixes, force-pushes the branch, and opens or updates that pull request. The body lists each fix with its exact location and the evidence it cites. When a run finds nothing left to fix, it closes the pull request instead of opening an empty one.

name: Offing fixes

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1" # Mondays 06:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: offing-fixes
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  fixes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: velella-sh/offing@v0.1.0
        with:
          fix-pr: "true"
          fail-on-severity: none

Every run force-pushes offing/fixes, and the pull request is found by its head branch rather than by title or body, so running twice updates the same pull request. A fixer that cannot apply a change exactly leaves that finding alone: the pull request contains only the patches that were applied. Review the pull request as you would any other; Offing never merges it and never touches the default branch.

fix-pr runs only on schedule and workflow_dispatch events. On any other event the Action logs a notice and leaves the repository alone, so a pull request from a fork, whose token is read-only, never tries to push. The scan itself stays offline: only the git push and the GitHub API calls that create, update, or close the pull request use the network, after the scan has finished. The job needs contents: write to push the branch and pull-requests: write to manage the pull request.

See it working on a schedule in offing-action-sample: it keeps one fix pull request and one tracking issue current every Monday.

Permissions and privacy

Only contents: read is required. Offing does not need pull-requests: write unless you set pr-comment: true, commands: true, or suggest-fixes: true; it then writes one pull request comment, command reply, or review of suggestions, each found again by a hidden marker and updated on every re-run, and needs only pull-requests: write for that. Offing does not send repository contents to an Offing backend. Annotations are emitted through runner workflow commands. tracking-issue: true needs issues: write; it updates one issue, also found by a hidden marker, and touches nothing else. With fix-pr: true it also needs contents: write (to push offing/fixes) and pull-requests: write (to open, update, or close the fix pull request).

The bundled scan is local and deterministic. When upload-report is true, the official actions/upload-artifact adapter sends offing-report.json to GitHub and retains it for 14 days. The report can contain repository-relative paths, matched source excerpts, dependency versions, and lifecycle evidence. Repository administrators should apply normal Actions artifact access controls or disable uploading for sensitive repositories.

Forked pull requests receive the same read-only scan behavior; no repository secrets are required.

README badge

Set upload-badge: true to generate offing-badge.json and offing-badge.svg and upload the offing-badge artifact, even when the severity gate fails. The badge-path output lets a later step publish the same file. This is opt-in and does not grant the Action write access or make network requests during the scan.

The badge reads offing | clean, or offing | 3 high when findings remain. The message counts findings after baseline comparison and names the highest remaining severity. It does not say a repository is risk-free: suppressed findings are excluded, and the severity gate can pass while lower-severity findings remain. stale means the lifecycle data is old (appended as · stale when findings remain), and expired means a baseline suppression expired under on-expired: fail. Colors come from the Offing palette: Verified Green for clean, muted amber for low and medium, red for high and critical.

offing-badge.svg is the finished badge with the Offing mark. The Shields.io endpoint format file, offing-badge.json, holds schemaVersion, label, message, color, and labelColor, for use with img.shields.io/endpoint when you want a different Shields style.

Actions artifacts require authentication, so their download URLs cannot be used as public Shields endpoints. For a public README, publish the JSON to a public URL, such as a dedicated branch in a public repository. This example reserves the offing-badge branch for the generated file; only trusted pushes to main and manual runs on main may publish. No pull-request code gets a write token. Use the default branch name of your repository if it is different.

name: Offing badge
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: write
concurrency:
  group: offing-badge
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  badge:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: velella-sh/offing@vX.Y.Z
        id: scan
        with:
          upload-badge: true
      - name: Publish aggregate badge data
        if: always() && steps.scan.outputs.badge-path != ''
        env:
          BADGE_PATH: ${{ steps.scan.outputs.badge-path }}
          BADGE_SVG_PATH: ${{ steps.scan.outputs.badge-svg-path }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          publish=$(mktemp -d)
          git init "$publish"
          git -C "$publish" remote add origin "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY.git"
          # GitHub CLI is preinstalled on ubuntu-latest.
          gh auth setup-git
          if git -C "$publish" ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin offing-badge; then
            git -C "$publish" fetch --depth=1 origin offing-badge
            git -C "$publish" checkout -b offing-badge FETCH_HEAD
          else
            git -C "$publish" checkout --orphan offing-badge
          fi
          cp "$BADGE_PATH" "$publish/offing-badge.json"
          cp "$BADGE_SVG_PATH" "$publish/offing-badge.svg"
          git -C "$publish" config user.name github-actions[bot]
          git -C "$publish" config user.email 41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com
          git -C "$publish" add offing-badge.json offing-badge.svg
          if ! git -C "$publish" diff --cached --quiet; then
            git -C "$publish" commit -m "chore: update Offing badge"
            git -C "$publish" push origin HEAD:offing-badge
          fi

Then add this to the README, replacing OWNER and REPO:

[![Offing lifecycle findings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OWNER/REPO/offing-badge/offing-badge.svg)](https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/actions)

Shields and GitHub cache badge images, so updates can take time to appear. The badge describes the last published scan, not the latest commit or a guarantee of freshness. A scan that cannot complete emits no new badge; its workflow failure remains the authoritative status. Schedule trusted scans if you need regular refreshes. Publishing aggregate counts makes them public; private repositories can keep the artifact private or deliberately publish only this aggregate file.

Code scanning

Set upload-sarif: true to show findings in the repository's Security → Code scanning tab. The Action writes the same findings as SARIF 2.1.0 and hands the file to github/codeql-action/upload-sarif under the category offing. The job needs one more permission:

permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write

steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v7
  - uses: velella-sh/offing@v0.1.0
    with:
      upload-sarif: true

The token of a pull request from a fork is read-only, so the upload would fail there. Enable it for pushes and for pull requests from the same repository, for example upload-sarif: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' }}. Code scanning is free for public repositories and needs GitHub Code Security on private ones. The SARIF carries only locations and Offing's own rule text, not source content; the mapping is below.

SARIF output

The same SARIF is available from the CLI, so other CI systems and editors can read it:

offing scan . --format sarif > offing.sarif

Output is deterministic: rules and results are sorted, paths are repository-relative with forward slashes on every platform, and neither the scan time nor the checkout path is written. Two scans of the same commit produce identical files.

SARIF Offing
tool.driver.name, version Offing and the installed version
rules[].id, name The lifecycle rule id, for example github-actions.checkout.node20
rules[].shortDescription The rule title
rules[].help (text and markdown) Replacement, deadline, migration steps, verification commands, and sources
rules[].helpUri The first evidence source
rules[].defaultConfiguration.level The same level mapping as results[].level, for the rule's severity
rules[].properties.tags lifecycle and the detector id
results[].ruleId, ruleIndex The finding's rule
results[].level critical and high → error; medium → warning; low and info → note
results[].message.text The finding summary, which names the exact reference, such as actions/checkout@v3
results[].locations[] File path (uriBaseId %SRCROOT%) and startLine when the finding has a line
results[].partialFingerprints["offingFindingId/v1"] The finding id, so alerts keep their identity between runs

JSON, text, annotations, and SARIF are renderings of the same findings. A finding suppressed by a baseline is absent from all of them.

Privacy. SARIF contains no source code: only file paths, line numbers, and Offing's own rule text and evidence links. It is uploaded only when upload-sarif is true, and then only to GitHub code scanning in the same repository. Nothing is sent to an Offing service.
